geometry_edits.rationale: Reduce the notch depth so the public threshold becomes a clearer seam tied to the access edge instead of a heavy bite.
Narrow the threshold incision to keep the dominant bar intact while preserving a legible entry void.
Calm the stepped upper mass so the section reads as one continuous inhabited gesture rather than a stack of arbitrary tiers.

rationale: The candidate reads coherently in all four views as one dominant bent bar with a notch-like public threshold, so it avoids the one-view-only failure. The parcel response is generally credible: the long mass aligns to the site frame and the carved edge reads as a usable open-space figure rather than a purely decorative subtraction. The blue frontage edge is acknowledged by a visible seam/void at the lower side, though the response is modest rather than especially generous. Program-wise, this can plausibly support neighborhood living because the mass remains compact, mixed-scale, and ground-responsive. The main weakness is sectional: the stepped/bent upper mass feels somewhat arbitrary and more sculptural than program-structural, with the upper terraces not fully explaining daylight, access, or a clearly inhabited roof sequence. So the form passes program fit, but only with a medium confidence on section-program relationship.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Elongated low-rise mass with a legible central void and a site-responsive horizontal spread.
Interlocking masses with bridges, setbacks, and a large courtyard/void that organizes public circulation.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More pavilion-like and smaller in scale than the candidate; limited relevance for this more articulated bent-bar mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact pavilion logic with a simple ground threshold and small vertical accent; useful as a minor edge-response reference.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual reference; its ramped/terraced waterfront condition is not the same access relationship as this parcel and should only inform sectional public-space logic.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/sectional massing can produce a strong inhabited roof edge and public-facing terrace sequence.

warnings: The stepped/bent upper condition risks reading as a decorative stack if further refined without a stronger roof/section logic.
Access-edge response is present but not strongly articulated; a more legible public seam or court would better satisfy the street-threshold invariant.
